blogs.title: Bits That Matter: How BitNet b1.58 Cuts LLM Costs by Three‑Fold
blogs.description: This post explains how moving every weight from FP16 down to tri‑state \,{-1\,,0\,,+1\} (a practical 1.58 bits per weight) dramatically saves GPU memory (≈ ⅓), speeds inference up (≈ 2–4×), and slashes arithmetic energy consumption over thirty‑times thanks to integer‐only matrix multiplies.

blogs.title: Quantizing Intuition – The absMean Ternary Formula Behind One‑Bit Layers
blogs.description: Dive into BitNet’s core quantizer that normalizes a weight matrix by its mean absolute value then rounds each element to \,{-1\,,0\,,+1\}. Discover why adding the zero state adds effective ‘feature filtering’ power and allows training straight from scratch while remaining fully compatible with standard Transformer backbones.

blogs.title: "LLaMA Meets One–Bit" – Integrating BitNet b1.58 Into Open–Source Pipelines
blogs.description: Learn how BitNet’s design reuses RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embeddings and omits biases so it plugs seamlessly into HuggingFace 🤗 tooling, vLLM inference engines and lightweight runners such as llama.cpp without rewriting front ends.

blogs.title: _Zero‑Shot Accuracy Versus Full Precision_ — Competitive Perplexity From Scaled Ternary Models
blogs.description: "The data speaks" — shows that whenever model size reaches around 3 B parameters Bitcoin’s b1.58 matches or exceeds FP16 baselines across ARC‑Easy/Challenge, Hellaswag and Winogrande tasks while keeping perplexity low enough for realistic language generation.

blogs.title: "MoE + One–Bit": A New Path Toward On‑Chip Expert Networks
blogs.description:
"Memory
is
a bottleneck" — explores how ternary weights shrink expert memories enough that multiple experts can live on a single chip, eliminates expensive inter‑node traffic common in current MoE deployments and paves the way for ultra‐lightweight switching.

blogs.title: _Hardware Tailored For Ternary Transformers_ — Designing LPUs That Only Add
blogs.description: "If your MACs don't multiply," explains why specialized units that perform fast integer add operations replace costly FP16 FUs in GPUs/ASICs can drastically improve throughput and reduce DRAM access latency when running bitnet models.
